newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada tobacco bill moves closer to becoming law.
newsitem.headline: Canada tobacco bill moves closer to becoming law.

text.p: A controversial Canadian bill that would restrict sponsorship by tobacco companies moved one step closer to becoming law on Thursday.
A Senate committee passed the bill without amendment, despite outspoken criticism from opposition Conservative senators.
The bill now heads to its third and final reading, expected some time this month, a Senate official said.

The bill proposes restrictions on tobacco advertising in public events. Proponents say limiting advertising and sponsorship will discourage smoking, especially among young people. But the bill's critics say the bill would rob popular sports and arts events, such as the Montreal Grand Prix, of their funding.
The unelected Senate is under pressure to pass the bill quickly since an election is likely to be called next month.
Imperial Tobacco Ltd, a unit of Imasco Ltd controls about 65 percent of the Canadian cigarette market. Imasco is 40 percent-owned by B.A.T Industries Plc of Britain.

The second biggest player, Rothmans, Benson and Hedges Inc, is 60 percent-owned by Rothmans Inc, a unit of Rothmans International Plc, owned by Swiss luxury goods holding company Cie Financiere Richmont AG, and 40 percent by Philip Morris Cos Inc.
Third-ranked RJR MacDonald is wholly owned by RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp unit R.J. Reynolds Tobacco International.
